name: CheatHere
tagline: A desktop AI overlay that reads your screen and the conversation and feeds you answers in real time during interviews and assessments.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible machinery here is not complicated: an always-on-top window, a screenshot every few seconds, a microphone and system audio tap, transcription, and a model call that streams a suggested answer. A competent agent will get you that in a weekend, and for legitimate uses like a screen-aware assistant while you work, it is genuinely fine. What you will not get in one sitting is the actual product, which is being invisible: staying out of screen shares, screen recordings and proctoring software while every vendor on the other side actively tries to catch you. That is a permanent cat-and-mouse maintenance job, not a build. Worth saying plainly: using any of this in a proctored exam or a live interview is fraud, and the failure mode is not a bug report, it is a rescinded offer.
coreLoopDIY: A local Electron overlay that captures your screen and the live audio, transcribes it, and streams a model-generated answer into a small always-on-top panel triggered by a hotkey.
requirements: macOS or Windows with screen recording and microphone permissions granted
A system audio loopback device if you want to hear the other side, for example BlackHole on macOS
Node 20 and comfort running an unsigned Electron app locally
whatYouLose: Invisibility: your overlay shows up in screen shares and recordings, which is the entire reason the paid thing exists
The ongoing anti-detection work against proctoring and monitoring tools, which changes monthly
Latency tuning, so your DIY answers land several awkward seconds late
Phone or second-device modes and prompt presets tuned to specific interview and exam formats
Someone else's legal exposure instead of yours
moatNotes: The moat is adversarial, not technical: whoever spends the most time reacting to proctoring vendors wins, and that is a treadmill nobody self-hosts.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the hard part is not the LLM call, it is the stealth and the speed. A rough overlay that answers in eight seconds and appears in the recording is worse than useless in the exact moment it is needed, and the paid tools exist purely to be fast and to not be there when someone looks. That is continuous maintenance against a moving target, and no personal build keeps up with it. The honest alternative to paying is not a weekend project, it is learning the material.
notes: The overlay is a weekend build; the stealth is a subscription to someone else's arms race. The moat is staying ahead of proctoring vendors, forever, on your behalf.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user desktop assistant called Overlay that watches my screen and the current conversation and drafts a suggested answer on demand. Use Electron plus TypeScript plus Vite plus React. No accounts, no cloud backend, no telemetry, no analytics.

In scope:
- A small always-on-top, frameless, transparent window, roughly 420x520, draggable, that can be shown and hidden with a global hotkey (Cmd+Shift+Space on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+Space elsewhere).
- A second hotkey that captures the current screen via desktopCapturer, downsizes it to max 1280px wide as JPEG, and sends it with the recent transcript to the model.
- Audio capture from the default microphone and, if the user selects a loopback input device, from that too. Chunk audio into 10 second WAV segments and transcribe with the OpenAI transcription API. Keep a rolling 5 minute transcript in memory only.
- One model call to gpt-4o-mini with the transcript tail plus the screenshot, streaming tokens into the panel as bullet points, not prose.
- A settings panel: API key status, input device pickers, hotkey display, a system prompt textarea persisted to a local JSON file in app userData.
- Everything in memory or on disk locally. A Clear button that wipes transcript, screenshots and history immediately.

Out of scope, do not implement: hiding the window from screen capture or screen sharing, evading or fingerprinting proctoring software, virtual cameras, driver level tricks, or any account system. If asked, the window is a normal visible window.

Secrets: read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env via dotenv in the main process only, never in the renderer. Ship .env.example.

Deliver: repo with npm run dev and npm run build, a README covering permissions setup on macOS (Screen Recording and Microphone) and loopback device setup, and a short LIMITATIONS section stating plainly that this overlay is visible in screen shares and recordings and that using it during exams or interviews is academic and professional fraud.
